# [L3 — The trend depends on the start year](../hypodrafts/L3.md "The trend depends on the start year")

*Generated by `scripts/pages/hypodraft_l3.py`: what the data held here can and cannot show about the hypothesis. Each marked statement links to what it rests on.*

**Status.** <span class="claim" data-claim="C-IL-L3-STATUS">The test this page specifies has not been run: no script in this repository computes it.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-IL-L3-STATUS "What this claim rests on")</sup>

## The observable consequence, stated so it can fail

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-IL-L3-READINGS">[L3](../hypodrafts/L3.md "The trend depends on the start year") has a weak reading and a strong reading, and only the strong one is a claim about the sea.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-IL-L3-READINGS "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-IL-L3-WEAK">**Weak:** *a slope fitted to a Danish series changes when you move the cut.* That is true of any noisy series, whatever the sea did, and is not worth testing.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-IL-L3-WEAK "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-IL-L3-STRONG">**Strong:** *the window-dependence exceeds what a single constant rate plus the series' own autocorrelated noise would produce* — i.e. the record contains genuinely different eras, so "the trend" is not a well-defined quantity and reporting one number is a category error.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-IL-L3-STRONG "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-IL-L3-FALSIFY">**Falsified if:** over the full space of admissible windows, the spread of fitted slopes, and the fraction of them that are positive, both fall inside the interval generated by simulating one constant slope with matched `AR(1)` noise. Then the window-dependence is noise around a single rate, the number is estimable, and [L3](../hypodrafts/L3.md "The trend depends on the start year")'s strong reading is not established for this variable.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-IL-L3-FALSIFY "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-IL-L3-SUPPORT">**Supported if:** the observed surface is more dispersed, or its sign-share further from a single-trend expectation, than that simulation allows.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-IL-L3-SUPPORT "What this claim rests on")</sup>

## The data held

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-IL-L3-PANEL">`docs/data/areas/stations_series.json` holds [679,422](../SOURCES.md#F-b61d7944ec) station-months, the sum of its [9](../SOURCES.md#F-81bea72caf) variables' counts, at [1,415](../SOURCES.md#F-fff0060a3d) stations, in [564](../SOURCES.md#F-008df4b99b) month slots from January [1980](../SOURCES.md#F-44433af5f2); `stations_series.bin` is [5,435,376](../SOURCES.md#F-91ec567fa1) bytes, [8](../SOURCES.md#F-5ccadf68a1) per station-month, as the declared layout of a `uint16` station index, a `uint16` month index and a `float32` value requires.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-IL-L3-PANEL "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-IL-L3-OXY">Variable used: **`oxy_bed`**, near-bed oxygen in mg/l: [76,980](../SOURCES.md#F-a95c664ddf) station-months at [1,327](../SOURCES.md#F-a053d110be) stations.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-IL-L3-OXY "What this claim rests on")</sup> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-IL-L3-RANGE">`stations_series.py` takes the median of every value in the deepest quarter of each cast's depth range, with no test of range, so values no instrument could give, which the extracts are known to carry, reach the panel; the flag record marks [11](../SOURCES.md#F-c8b8b1dcfd) station-months at [6](../SOURCES.md#F-4ed890d0d9) stations as a sign inversion ([I7](../HYPOTHESES.md "Batch defects in ingest or processing")) and removes nothing. A test must set its own bounds and say how many values they drop.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-IL-L3-RANGE "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-IL-L3-STRUCT">Two further faults are structural and are not fixed, only declared. The panel is a monthly median per station, so within-month spread and any daily oxygen cycle are gone from it, and the CTD extract it is built from carries a date and no hour.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-IL-L3-STRUCT "What this claim rests on")</sup> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-IL-L3-RESID">Both inflate the year-to-year residual; the null below is matched to the residual actually observed, so they widen the null rather than being smuggled into the signal.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-IL-L3-RESID "What this claim rests on")</sup> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-IL-L3-SATCHK">The saturation cross-check uses `oxysat_bed`, which is computed from oxygen, temperature and salinity, and is reported as a robustness check only.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-IL-L3-SATCHK "What this claim rests on")</sup>

## The constraint, and therefore the null

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-IL-L3-CONSTR">Constraint: annual index years **[1989](../SOURCES.md#F-88318bec13)–[2025](../SOURCES.md#F-ee5510914b)** ([37](../SOURCES.md#F-24d6de13e2) years), windows of **at least [10](../SOURCES.md#F-bb2ec6e7ca) years**, giving **[406](../SOURCES.md#F-0413276518) admissible windows**.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-IL-L3-CONSTR "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-IL-L3-INDEX">Index = two-way fixed effects (station + calendar month, alternating demeaning to convergence), then the annual mean of residuals.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-IL-L3-INDEX "What this claim rests on")</sup> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-IL-L3-LEVELS">Station effects absorb level differences, so composition change in *levels* cannot drive the index.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-IL-L3-LEVELS "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-IL-L3-NULLPROC">**The null is not "zero sensitivity".** For each station set, estimate ρ and σ from the detrended index, then simulate [4,000](../SOURCES.md#F-74d5587d92) `AR(1)` series of the same length and compute the same [406](../SOURCES.md#F-0413276518)-window surface. Two nulls:</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-IL-L3-NULLPROC "What this claim rests on")</sup>

- <span class="claim" data-claim="C-IL-L3-H0">**`H0`, no trend at all.** Each window's slope is then noise, as likely positive as negative, so finding both signs across the windows is expected with no trend at all: *a sign flip on its own does not tell a trend from none.*</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-IL-L3-H0 "What this claim rests on")</sup>
- <span class="claim" data-claim="C-IL-L3-H1">**`H1`, one constant slope equal to the fitted full-window slope, plus matched noise.** This is the null that [L3](../hypodrafts/L3.md "The trend depends on the start year")'s strong reading must beat.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-IL-L3-H1 "What this claim rests on")</sup>

## The two confounds

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-IL-L3-COMP">**Composition.** If the stations reporting change over the record ([I1](../hypodrafts/I1.md "Changing station network")), station effects absorb their levels but not their seasonal timing. A split into summer-peaked and year-round stations must then state its rule, including a minimum number of observations: a station seen in a single calendar month has a seasonal resultant of exactly one by construction, and would count as perfectly seasonal.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-IL-L3-COMP "What this claim rests on")</sup> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-IL-L3-CORE">The test is to be repeated on a fixed core of stations reporting throughout the index period, which a change of composition cannot move.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-IL-L3-CORE "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-IL-L3-SAT">**Thermometer.** The same surface can be computed on `oxysat_bed` ([64,493](../SOURCES.md#F-1f76a99b02) station-months at [1,152](../SOURCES.md#F-85ccdc820d) stations): oxygen as a share of what the water holds at saturation, at its temperature and salinity. A decline in concentration that is absent in saturation points to solubility rather than oxygen supply. Not computed here.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-IL-L3-SAT "What this claim rests on")</sup>

Nothing is licensed yet.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-IL-L3-LICENSE "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-IL-L3-NOTLIC">Not licensed: anything about chlorophyll, nutrient loading, or the modelled reference condition, which is where [L3](../hypodrafts/L3.md "The trend depends on the start year")'s stake actually lies ([L1](../HYPOTHESES.md "The reference condition never existed"), [L2](../HYPOTHESES.md "The reference is a model output treated as a fact")). Nothing causal.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-IL-L3-NOTLIC "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-IL-L3-PRE">Nor anything before the panel's first year, [1980](../SOURCES.md#F-44433af5f2), which `cube.py` fixes: the CTD extract it is built from holds station-days with temperature and salinity from [1970](../SOURCES.md#F-cf77feeaa1), and those earlier years are not in the panel. [L3](../hypodrafts/L3.md "The trend depends on the start year") is about where monitoring records begin, so the earlier years matter to it.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-IL-L3-PRE "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-IL-L3-SLOPE">Whatever the result, a single slope is not licensed on its own: any published rate needs its window and its `H1` interval printed beside it.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-IL-L3-SLOPE "What this claim rests on")</sup>
